title: FlexRL 1.0.1 (release candidate)
text: Bugs fixed. Performance: Gibbs machinery ~100x faster end--end benchmark problem (review/bench-stem.R, nA=10000, nB=15000, n_links=7500, 22 sweeps: 238.7 s -> 2.29 s); 100k/150k-record problem (75k links, 22 sweeps) serial run takes 88 s threads = 8 brings ~51 s. candidate-pair log-likelihood now plain per-pair vector (nA x nB sparse matrix data-frame row subsetting gone), candidate pairs built single C++ call (buildCandidatePairs()), per-sweep likelihood pieces computed one fused C++ pass (pairLogLik()), sampleL samples joint (H^, H^B) exact O(nval) factorization, kernels draw pre-drawn uniform blocks. sampleD() signature now (S, LLA, LLB, LLL, gamma, nlinkrec, links, threads). gamma single scalar; linkage state passed links, 0-based k x 2 matrix (, B) record pairs (0x2 nothing linked), replacing sumRowD/sumColD arguments — flags derived links still returned. return list gains links (updated 0-based pairs) next linksQ (1-based rows S); loglik dropped inputs (value cancels every acceptance ratio reconstructed internally). simulateD() likewise takes current linksR sumRowD/sumColD; gains threads model_dynamics. global C++ link map — initDeltaMap() Deltafind() — gone: sweep carries state calls, everything needs lives arguments. sampleNL() takes unif argument; sampleL() takes (survivalpSameH, nval, phikA, phikB, eta, unif) returns joint (H^, H^B) matrix. Kernels draw Uniform(0,1) deviates pre-drawn blocks consumed pair position rather calling RNG per draw: given set.seed() realised draws differ <= 1.0.0 (distributions ). OpenMP: per-pair likelihood loops Gibbs kernels parallelised; new threads argument StEM() (default 4; build without OpenMP code runs sequentially regardless). Results bitwise identical thread count. package still builds — runs sequentially — platforms without OpenMP. built-survival models (exponential, Weibull, Gompertz, piecewise) evaluate fused, parallel C++ kernel (survivalS_cpp) instead R-level matrix algebra; custom survival functions unaffected keep working exactly . Values agree previous R implementation ~1e-16 (BLAS rounding); survival_model() objects gain cuts field. Parity verified pre-optimisation implementation pinned permanent regression tests: tests/testthat/test-golden-parity.R compares current kernels golden fixtures generated pre-optimisation build (review/generate-goldens.R, baseline glm-notes @ 4b09088) — likelihoods candidate-pair sets exactly, StEM seed clouds tiny problem’s stationary frequencies Monte-Carlo level. See review/PARITY-REPORT.md.
